counterfactual.change: Feasible but slow at 22 months; no biomarker relaxation reaches 18 months (all-comers gives 19). Comfortable enrolment would need ~85 sites at the current marker.

drivers: exclusion of other causes of esophageal eosinophilia (hypereosinophilic syndrome, Churg-Strauss/EGPA, parasitic infection, celiac, Crohn's, achalasia)
esophageal stricture precluding endoscope passage or requiring dilation
washout/stability requirements for PPIs, topical/systemic corticosteroids, and prior biologics (esp. exclusion of prior anti-IL-4R/dupilumab exposure)
requirement for symptomatic dysphagia frequency/severity thresholds
exclusion for concomitant EG/EoD or eosinophilic colitis and other GI comorbidities
eligibility.reasoning: Across EoE trials, the biomarker-positive population is further reduced by exclusions for alternative causes of eosinophilia, structural esophageal disease, recent steroid/biologic use, and symptom/dysphagia entry thresholds (NCT03029091, NCT02227836, NCT03191864, NCT04322708). These stacked but only partially overlapping criteria typically remove roughly half of biomarker-positive patients.

failedPrecedents.whyStopped: Inability to complete enrollment due to difficulty in finding subjects

High-level results from the MESSINA Phase III trial showed that AstraZeneca's Fasenra (benralizumab) did not meet one of the two dual-primary endpoints. Given the lack of clear benefit in this patient population, study has been terminated.

poweringBasis: phase-3 precedent median (23 trials) floors the effect size d=0.8 estimate of 65
why: 159 patients (phase-3 precedent median (23 trials) floors the effect size d=0.8 estimate of 65) at 69 sites (p75 of at-scale precedents); precedent velocity 0.46 pt/site/mo across 91 completed trials, narrowed by 85% biomarker prevalence and 55% eligibility pass rate, with ~13 interventional trials competing for the same patients.
